controls: Bound evidence bytes, prefix listing, repeated range reads, storage consumption, and startup-probe cleanup.
Reject anonymous access, wildcard credentials, wildcard CORS, exposed administration APIs, and default-service confusion.
Redact secrets, physical object keys, direct-upload targets, same-origin handles, and storage administration identities.
Retain auditable migration inventories, compatibility outcomes, lifecycle transitions, and operator-attributed destructive actions.
Bind service identity, credentials, bucket ownership, upload targets, and migration endpoints to explicit configuration.
Verify object digests, bucket/key identity, migration copy results, immutable compatibility cases, and retained artifact integrity.

storage_ref_controls.assertion: User-authored external locators are preserved and never rewritten as server-managed object references.
Malformed physical keys fail as object_store_invalid_request before an object-store call.
The canonical backend-neutral server reference is object://{object_blob_uuid}.
Object-store migration preserves bucket, physical key, and logical storage reference without mutating database identity.
Physical keys use lowercase RFC 4122 identities, slash-separated ASCII, no empty segments, and no NUL, CR, or LF.
Physical keys are at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes.
object_blobs.storage_key is a private physical bucket-relative object key.
Client writes of reserved_server_managed_ref fail as invalid_mutation_payload.
